title: Backward-compatibility contracts for pinned model versions (prompt formats, outputs, params)
creator: Ari Patel
description:
Problem: Customers pin model versions to guarantee stable outputs for downstream logic. Changes in prompt tokenization, default parameter semantics, or output structure from model upgrades or image/ops optimizations have caused subtle regressions and integration breakages. We need an engineering contract that guarantees backward compatibility for pinned model versions and publishes a machine-readable performance profile for each pinned version.

Goals:
- Define a formal compatibility contract (input prompt schemas, default parameter semantics, structured output schema, error codes).
- Ensure runtime enforces contract for any request that references a pinned model version (model_id@pin).
- Publish a JSON-based performance profile alongside the pinned version containing latency distributions, throughput SLOs, memory/kv usage expectations, and token counting rules.
- Provide test harnesses and CI gates for model onboarding that validate compatibility before publishing a pin.

Proposal (high level):
1) Contract format: a top-level JSON artifact stored alongside model metadata with fields: "prompt_schema" (free-form, with example templates), "response_schema" (strict JSON Schema string for structured outputs when applicable), "parameter_spec" (defaults, permitted ranges, and semantic notes for temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop sequences, streaming behavior), "tokenization" (vocab/model tokenizer version + token counting rules), and "compatibility_level" (major|min|patch style semantics). This artifact is versioned (semver-like) and immutable once a pin is published.
2) Runtime enforcement: When requests use a pinned model identifier, server will: a) validate user parameters against parameter_spec; b) optionally normalize prompts according to prompt_schema (with opt-out); c) ensure the top-level output shape matches response_schema if provided; d) if the model deviates, log as contract-violation, block (for P0-level violations), or fallback according to the pin's rollback policy.
3) Publishing workflow: On model onboarding, model-owners/ops submit a model-package with candidate contract artifact. CI runs the compatibility harness: deterministic prompt replay, randomized fuzzing within parameter ranges, and throughput/latency profiling. The model is green if no contract violations for defined critical prompt set and performance metrics meet published thresholds.
4) Performance profile: a machine-readable JSON with percentiles (p50, p95, p99) for end-to-end latency by input-length buckets, per-token generation latency, memory footprint under steady-state batching, recommended batching and cache window settings, and expected cost-per-1M tokens under quantization profiles. This profile is surfaced in the Console and available via the API for customers to make routing decisions.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Risks:
- Overly strict enforcement could break legitimate progressive model improvements; need staged enforcement and a rollback policy.
- Schema drift when models start emitting richer outputs; include a path for additive schema evolution (non-breaking additions allowed; breaking changes require new pin).
- Performance profile variability across hardware; must include metadata for target hardware (instance family) and test harness must run on representative & documented hardware.

Open questions: 
- Do we support auto-conversion layers to map new outputs to old schema for minor changes? (proposal: support opt-in shim transforms maintained by model-ops).
- How do we classify compatibility levels exactly (major/minor/patch rules)?
- Which violations should be "block publish" vs "warn"?

Next steps:
- Draft JSON contract schema and sample artifact (owner: Nina).
- Implement CI harness skeleton in onboarding repo (owner: ENG-sre pairing).
- Add console UI surface for pin artifact and perf profile (PM+Design spike).
- Schedule security review for tokenization and KMS handling of model artifacts.

Estimated effort: 8 points across runtime, CI, and onboarding UX.
acceptance_criteria: Contract artifact schema published and stored immutable with model pin
Runtime enforces parameter_spec and tokenization rules for pinned model requests
A CI harness that runs deterministic prompt set and fuzz tests before pin approval
Performance profile JSON published with p50/p95/p99 latency per input-length bucket and included hardware metadata
Console shows pin contract and perf profile; API exposes profile via /models/{id}/pins/{pin}/profile
Documentation with migration guidance and rollback policy published
